idea-plugin.name: Basalt
idea-plugin.description:
Razor views written in Visual Basic, in Rider.

ASP.NET Core's Razor compiler emits C# and only C#. A .vbhtml file — a real file type in ASP.NET before Core — has no compiler and no editor support anywhere. This plugin is the editing half.

What it does

  • Completion, including the members of the view's model: type @Model. and the properties of the class are offered, read from the project as the compiler sees it.
  • Diagnostics as you type, reported against the view and the line you wrote — not against generated code.
  • Hover with the signature and documentation of whatever is under the pointer.
  • Go to definition, from a name in the markup through to the .vb file that declares it.
  • Signature help, folding and the document outline.

What it needs

A solution or a .vbproj in the folder you open: the plugin's language server compiles the project to answer about types, and finds one on its own. Opening a single loose file gives markup support and nothing more — honestly so, rather than guessing.

Compiling the views

Editing is not building. Add the Basalt.Razor.Vb NuGet package to the project and every .vbhtml is compiled by a source generator into Visual Basic, alongside the rest of the code. Errors then arrive at build time, at the right line of the view.

The same server backs the Visual Studio and VS Code extensions, so a view reads the same in all three.
